objective: Turn stock history, graph relationships, and conditional Monte Carlo forecasts into an interactive time-aware 3D research lab, then test whether motion-derived variables, loss functions, and activation functions improve sealed-holdout-safe predictions.

visual_labs.description: An animated 3D universe with a date slider, play/pause controls, selectable trails, hover explanations, and synchronized portfolio diagnostics.

A stock-level animated probability tube showing simulated return percentiles, target and stop-loss hit probabilities, expected shortfall, realized path overlays, and neighbor/regime-conditioned alternatives.
A 3D graph layout whose node trails reveal cluster migration, crowding, divergence, contagion, and regime transitions through time.

requirements: Fit every distribution and regime boundary on training rows only.
Preserve serial dependence with moving blocks.
Report target-hit, stop-hit, expected return, expected shortfall, and calibration.
Do not treat simulated paths as new independent training observations.

loss_function_ablation.purpose: combine probability quality with differentiable return utility, turnover penalty, and downside-risk penalty
loss_function_ablation.guardrail: Tune utility weights only inside nested training validation and compare against pure BCE.

experimental_controls.sealed_holdout_rule: Do not open until the visual features and model family are frozen.

feature_acceptance_gate.rule: A visually inspired variable is retained only if its pre-registered leave-one-feature-out result improves at least two of ranking, calibration, or after-cost return without a material risk deterioration across chronological splits.
prohibitions: Do not promote a feature because its animation looks persuasive.
Do not select variables using the sealed final holdout.
Do not infer causality from spatial proximity in a learned projection.
